paper.title: Additive Causal Bandits with Unknown Graph

settings.name_in_paper: Causal bandit with an unknown graph (CBUG) (lower bound)
unmapped: Causal graph over discrete variables is unknown; actions are interventions do(X=x) on any subset of variables (global interventions allowed)
No latent confounders between Y and its ancestors
settings.definition_quote: We consider the causal bandit problem in the setting where $\graph$ is unknown and the learner must find, for $\epsilon>0$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, an $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PAC solution ... We assume that $Y\cond\doi(\X=\x)$ is 1-sub-Gaussian for any intervention.

settings.name_in_paper: Additive CBUG / additive combinatorial linear bandit with full-bandit feedback (unknown number of parents)
unmapped: Actions are global interventions: Cartesian product choosing one value in [M_k] for each of K discrete variables (one-hot encoding, d = sum_k M_k)
Outcome is additive in the parents of Y: Y = sum_k f_k(X_k) + eta
Learner knows a bound B_rng on the scale of the outcome effects (input B)
Causal graph unknown; no latent confounders between Y and its ancestors
settings.definition_quote: There exist functions $f_1,\ldots, f_{\numPar}$ and a $\sigma^2$-sub-Gaussian random variable $\eta$ such that $Y = \sum_{k=1}^{\numPar} f_k(X_k) + \eta$.

settings.name_in_paper: Additive CBUG with known number of parents P_Y
unmapped: Actions are global interventions: Cartesian product choosing one value in [M_k] for each of K discrete variables
Outcome is additive in the parents of Y
The learner knows the number of parents P_Y of Y
Learner knows a bound B_rng on the scale of the outcome effects (input B)
settings.definition_quote: We also consider the case when $\calP_Y$ is provided, which allows termination once $\calP_Y$ variables have their optimal value identified.

symbols.N_pa: |supp(pa(Y))|, number of joint value configurations of the parents of Y

conditions: exists an instance (needle-in-haystack: mean flat except at one parent configuration); proof uses Bernoulli(1/2 + eps*1{q(x)=x_pa}) outcomes

source.label: thm:lower.bound
source.quote: There is an instance of the CBUG problem such that any $(\epsilon,\delta)$-PAC algorithm must take $\Omega\left(\frac{\left|\supp(\pa(Y))\right|}{\epsilon^2}\logf{1}{\delta}\right)$ samples in expectation.

results.notes: Existential lower bound (one hard instance). Proof sketch via Lattimore-Szepesvari Thm 33.5; proof writes O(.) loosely.

symbols.Delta_ki: per-variable gap Delta_k^i = max_j theta_k^j - theta_k^i of value i of variable X_k
symbols.B_rng: input bound B on the effect scale (paper's B)
symbols.sum_arms: here: sum over all variables k=1..K and values i=1..M_k

conditions: no latent confounders between Y and its ancestors

source.label: thm:sample.complexity
source.quote: Algorithm~\ref{algorithm:MODL} is $(\epsilon,\delta)$-PAC. The expected sample complexity has an upper bound of \frac{16\sigma^2}{3} \logf{\logf{BK}{\epsilon}}{\delta}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^{M_k}\frac{1}{(\Delta_{\min} \vee \Delta_k^i\vee\frac{\epsilon}{K})^2}, where $\Delta_{\min}$ ... is the minimum gap in the parents in the case when number of parents $\calP_Y$ is provided, and $0$ otherwise.

results.notes: Main-text statement; appendix restatement uses wedge (min) instead of vee and splits parents/non-parents (non-parents contribute M_k/epsilon^2 terms), inconsistent. Also delivers (epsilon,delta)-PAC guarantee.

symbols.Delta_ki: per-variable gap Delta_k^i of value i of variable X_k
symbols.B_rng: input bound B on the effect scale (paper's B)
symbols.sum_arms: here: sum over all variables k and values i in [M_k]
symbols.Delta_min: minimum gap among the parents: min_{k<=P_Y} min_i Delta_k^i (paper definition)

conditions: no latent confounders between Y and its ancestors
tuning: upper bound on P_Y supplied to the algorithm

source.label: thm:sample.complexity
source.quote: Algorithm~\ref{algorithm:MODL} is $(\epsilon,\delta)$-PAC. The expected sample complexity has an upper bound of ... where $\Delta_{\min} = \min_{k\leq \calP_Y}\min_{i\in [M_k]}\Delta_k^i$ is the minimum gap in the parents in the case when number of parents $\calP_Y$ is provided

results.notes: Paper's Delta_min is the min gap among parent values (redeclared). Appendix version has an extra K^2 factor and wedge instead of vee; recorded main-text version.

conditions: exists eps_min > 0 such that for every parent k there are i,i' with |f_k(i)-f_k(i')| >= eps_min

source.label: thm:recovering.parents
source.quote: Assume that there is some $\epsilon_{\min}>0$ such that, for all $k\leq \calP_Y$, there exist $i, i'\in[M_k]$ with $|f_k(i)-f_k(i')|\geq \epsilon_{\min}$. Let $\hat\x$ and $\hat\theta$ be the output of Algorithm~\ref{algorithm:MODL} run with $\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{\min}$ and $\delta>0$. Then $\widehat\pa(Y)$ as defined above has $\prob(\widehat\pa(Y) = \pa(Y))\geq 1-\delta$. Furthermore, the intervention ... is $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PAC.

results.notes: Bound on probability of incorrect parent-set recovery (<= delta); also states restricted intervention is (eps,delta)-PAC.
